claims.text: The rule, stated so a gate can test it: (1) a landform name (peak, ridge, knoll, rock, hill) is carried only by a landform-class label (name, plus ▲ and height where the DEM supplies one), never by a pin or by a venue name that embeds a landform word; (2) a venue or POI pin never counts as the landform's name for the hand-test landform-label recall or the named-heights count; (3) a pin may sit beside a landform label but never replaces it at any zoom or sheet. Plate two's peak-icon pins are the grey case: they keep the name but lose ▲, height and ink class, so they are read as a degraded landform label, not as a POI, and the table map must not copy them.

evidence.ref: research-dossier.md#'Lesson for the forbidden lists' (a POI pin must never stand in for a landform name); todo-inputs.json#reusable_facts.research[forbidden-list lesson]

claims.text: The rule is already half-encoded in Job 1 ruling R1: 'once arrived a name or height is never dropped, generalized or replaced by a pin at closer zoom', and R2 (one ink and one face family for landform and homestead names; rank decides when, not how). The new item for the bible is the venue-name clause (a name embedded in a venue pin does not count) and the plate-two peak-icon exception.

Where the gates already measure it: the Job 3 hand test passes only with landform-label recall >= 70% and >= 6 named heights outside the mask, counted from landform labels (bare integers and '<name> <integer>' entries), so a name that survives only inside a pin or venue label would not satisfy those counts if the capture lists landform labels only. The spec should say so explicitly.

Shipped example of the rule biting: the Epēshu city-chart POI list (19 numbered POIs, maps-site/data/chart-pois.json key Epēshu) carries three landforms as pins/halos: #17 Mount Mastery (chart px 246,121; 'tallest hill overlooking the harbor'), #18 Bangeph Rock (729,1082; 'tall, smooth tine of stone'), #19 The Fairy Arch (2852,2627). #16 Old Quarry Lot (1417,3835) is a site, not a landform. The sim carries the same names as extraLandmarks of kind 'label'/'spike' (not pins). None of the three falls in city quarter Q1 [256,2304)x[1280,3328). On the table map these names must be drawn as landform labels with ▲/height, with the POI halo remaining a separate hover-only layer.

No gazetteer name in a non-landform kind embeds a landform word (mount/mountain/hill/rock/ridge/peak/tor/knoll/crag/fell/cliff/bluff/height), and the only 3 'Mountains and Hills' markers are Far Mountains, Fell Mountains and Mountain Wall; so no atlas settlement or POI currently stands in for a landform name outside the Epēshu chart list above. Rule 2 must still bind the minted names (NAME.peak vs NAME.place) so a generated venue never reuses a ridge name.

gaps: Plates two and three are not registered to plate one's frame (different crops and scales); which plate-one landforms lie inside each frame is not established, so 'deleted' is counted as absent from the visible frame, not as proved removal at the same location.

Clipped labels cannot be read: plate two 'rve' (top-left; possibly a reserve or preserve name), KORBEL's full extent; plate three 'K' and 'Northwood C...' at the right edge, 'Seaview' left edge. Not guessed.

Whether plate two's peak-icon pins (Queens Peak, Pole Mountain, Neeley Hill) count as 'POI pins' under the owner's rule or as degraded landform labels is an interpretation; the brief only says 'a retreat pin' for plate three. The spec author or owner should confirm the grey-case reading in q02-c12.

Chart-px to atlas-px (or EPESHU_HF cell) positions of Mount Mastery, Bangeph Rock and The Fairy Arch are not computed here, so it is not established whether they fall inside the DEM window [1060,1240]..[1860,2040] and can receive a DEM height; outside it R22 forbids inventing relief.
The exact colours and font faces of plates two/three pins and labels were not sampled; only classes, positions and counts were read from the images.
The brief names no source for the quoted 'Almost every name does not' beyond the caption; nothing further about how the plates were captured (zoom level, provider) is available in the repo.
summary: Plate two keeps 3 peak-icon pins, 3 park pins, 4 place labels and 3 water names but no heights, glyphs, trails, washes or shields; plate three keeps about 12 place labels, 3 pins, 3 shields, built-up fills and park labels but no peaks, heights or water names, so landform names go from 27 on plate one to 3 pins to 0. The Black Mountain case (landform on plate one, absent on plate two, surviving only inside the 'Black Mountain Retreat Center' pin on plate three) fixes the rule: a landform name is carried only by a landform-class label, never by a pin or a venue name containing a landform word. In the repo the rule bites on the Epēshu chart POIs Mount Mastery, Bangeph Rock and The Fairy Arch, and it extends Job 1 ruling R1.
